review_title: Influenza vaccines for preventing cardiovascular disease
screening_criteria: Randomised controlled trials (RCTs) of influenza vaccination compared with placebo or no treatment in participants with or without cardiovascular disease, assessing cardiovascular death or non‐fatal cardiovascular events.
gold_label_policy_description: dataset label 1.0 counts as INCLUDE; 0.5 and 0.0 count as EXCLUDE

studies.study_title: Efficacy and safety of a live attenuated influenza vaccine in adults 60 years of age and older
studies.predicted_reason: This is an RCT of influenza vaccine vs placebo in elderly adults, but the outcomes assessed are influenza efficacy, immunogenicity, and safety only. No cardiovascular death or cardiovascular events were measured.

studies.study_title: The efficacy of influenza vaccination in elderly individuals. A randomized double‐blind placebo‐controlled trial
studies.predicted_reason: This is an RCT of influenza vaccine vs placebo in elderly people, but outcomes are limited to serological and clinical influenza incidence. No cardiovascular outcomes were assessed.

studies.study_title: Dose‐sparing H5N1 A/Indonesia/05/2005 pre‐pandemic influenza vaccine in adults and elderly adults: A phase III, placebo‐controlled, randomized study
studies.predicted_reason: This is an RCT of H5N1 prepandemic vaccine vs placebo, but outcomes are immunogenicity, cross-reactivity, and safety. No cardiovascular death or events were assessed.

studies.study_title: Influenza vaccination reduces cardiovascular events in patients with acute coronary syndrome
studies.predicted_reason: This is a PROBE study (prospective randomized open with blinded endpoint) comparing influenza vaccine vs no treatment in patients with acute coronary syndrome (CVD population). The primary endpoint was combined major cardiovascular events including death, hospitalization from ACS, heart failure, and stroke. Meets all selection criteria.

studies.study_title: A rapid immune response to 2009 influenza a(H1N1) vaccines in adults: a randomized, double‐blind, controlled trial
studies.predicted_reason: This is an RCT evaluating immunogenicity and safety of H1N1 vaccines. Outcomes are seroprotection rates and adverse reactions. No cardiovascular outcomes were assessed.

studies.study_title: Is influenza vaccination cost effective for healthy people between ages 65 and 74 years? A randomised controlled trial
studies.predicted_reason: This is an RCT of influenza vaccine vs placebo in healthy elderly people, but outcomes are influenza frequency and cost-effectiveness indicators. No cardiovascular death or events were assessed.

studies.study_title: Antibody response to influenza vaccine in coronary artery disease: a substudy of the FLUCAD study
studies.predicted_reason: This is a substudy of an RCT focusing on humoral immune response (antibody levels) in patients with coronary artery disease. While the parent study may have assessed cardiovascular outcomes, this substudy only reports immunogenicity data.

studies.study_title: Effect of influenza and pneumococcal vaccines in elderly persons in years of low influenza activity
studies.predicted_reason: This is an observational prospective study using administrative database data, not an RCT. Although it mentions cardiac failure outcomes, the study design does not meet the RCT requirement.

studies.study_title: An open‐label comparison of the immunogenicity and tolerability of intranasal and intramuscular formulations of virosomal influenza vaccine in healthy adults
studies.predicted_reason: This is an RCT comparing intranasal vs intramuscular influenza vaccine formulations in healthy adults. Outcomes are immunogenicity and adverse events. No cardiovascular outcomes were assessed.

studies.study_title: High‐dose trivalent influenza vaccine compared to standard dose vaccine in elderly adults: safety, immunogenicity and relative efficacy during the 2009‐2010 season
studies.predicted_reason: This is an RCT comparing high-dose vs standard-dose influenza vaccine in elderly adults. Outcomes are safety, immunogenicity, and influenza efficacy. No cardiovascular death or events were assessed.

studies.study_title: Comparison of the safety and immunogenicity of 2 respiratory syncytial virus (rsv) vaccines‐‐nonadjuvanted vaccine or vaccine adjuvanted with alum‐‐given concomitantly with influenza vaccine to high‐risk elderly individuals
studies.predicted_reason: This is an RCT primarily evaluating RSV vaccines given with influenza vaccine. Outcomes are humoral responses to RSV and influenza. No cardiovascular death or events were assessed.

studies.study_title: Lack of effect of influenza and pneumococcal vaccines on anticoagulation by warfarin
studies.predicted_reason: This is a single-blind controlled study (not fully randomized) investigating vaccine effects on warfarin anticoagulation. Outcomes are INR values and anticoagulant control. No cardiovascular death or events were assessed.

studies.study_title: [Impact of an anti‐flu vaccination strategy for prevention of cardiovascular diseases]
studies.predicted_reason: This is a before-after experimental study with a control group, not an RCT. It evaluates vaccination campaign strategies and coverage rates, not cardiovascular outcomes from vaccination.

studies.study_title: Influenza vaccination is associated with a reduced risk of stroke
studies.predicted_reason: This is a case-control study (370 stroke patients vs 370 controls), not an RCT. Although it assesses stroke risk, the study design does not meet the RCT requirement.

studies.study_title: [Secondary prevention of coronary artery disease. Flu vaccinations and new evidence of the role of infection in acute coronary syndromes]
studies.predicted_reason: This is a prospective randomized study (single-blind) comparing influenza vaccine vs control in myocardial infarction patients and PCI patients (CVD population). Primary outcomes include cardiovascular death and composite ischemic events. Meets all selection criteria.

studies.study_title: Comparison of two vaccination programmes in preventing influenza‐related hospitalization among the elderly during two consecutive seasons
studies.predicted_reason: This is an ecological/comparative study comparing vaccination programs across municipalities, not an RCT. Although it mentions cardiovascular hospitalizations, the study design does not meet the RCT requirement.

studies.study_title: Immune response to influenza vaccination in community‐dwelling Chinese elderly persons
studies.predicted_reason: This is an RCT of influenza vaccine vs placebo in elderly persons, but primary outcomes are immunogenicity (seroprotection rates, GMTs). While unplanned hospital admissions were reported, they were not specifically cardiovascular events.

studies.study_title: Influenza vaccination and vitamin K antagonist treatment: a placebo‐controlled, randomized, double‐blind crossover study
studies.predicted_reason: This is an RCT of influenza vaccine vs placebo in patients on warfarin, but primary outcomes are INR values and warfarin dose stability. Minor bleeding events were noted but these are not cardiovascular death or non-fatal cardiovascular events as defined in the protocol.

studies.study_title: Safety of a trivalent live attenuated intranasal influenza vaccine, FluMist, administered in addition to parenteral trivalent inactivated influenza vaccine to seniors with chronic medical conditions

studies.study_title: Decrease of progressing chronic heart failure and rheumatic heart disease by vaccination of patients against influenza
